**Continuous 2.16.1**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.16.1.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.16.1.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.16.1.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.16.1.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.16.1.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.16.1.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.16.1.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.16.1-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.16.1.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.16.1-vscode/continuous-cli-2.16.1.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.16.0

**This release closes gaps where a setting or a file said one thing and the agent did another.** A broken `permissions.yaml` or hook file no longer reads as "no policy", "always allow" no longer rewrites a file it could not load, an `--agent` file can only take tools away, and an MCP server's read-only hint counts only for a server you trust. Commands the agent runs can no longer wait for a prompt and report their real exit codes. The terminal agent gets recovery tools (`continuous doctor config`, `--safe`, `continuous reset`), a JSON event stream and exit codes for headless runs, masked session export and attention notifications; the chat input accepts dragged files, folders and images, and the Explorer and tab menus can add files to the chat. Read Behaviour changes first: several of them refuse what 2.16.0 allowed.

### Behaviour changes

**A broken hook settings file or `permissions.yaml` is not "no policy".** (#739)

- **A hook settings file or `permissions.yaml` that is present but broken no longer reads as "no policy".** Before, a hook settings file that did not parse was skipped with a log line (so a guard hook silently did not run), and a `permissions.yaml` that did not parse was treated as absent (so a headless run fell back to defaults that allow `Bash`). Now `cn -p` and `cn serve` refuse to start with exit code 2, naming each file and the line and column of the error (never its contents); `--ignore-broken-config` continues with the file ignored. The interactive agent starts and prints a visible WARNING with the same details. Absent files are still silent. See the Hooks and trust and Permissions pages.
- **A hook `matcher` that is not a valid regular expression now runs the hook** (fail closed) and warns once per session, instead of silently switching the hook off.

**Data-loss and recovery fixes in the terminal agent.** (#783)

- **The terminal agent's "always allow" no longer rewrites a `permissions.yaml` it could not load.** Before, when the file existed but was malformed or had a key the loader does not know, the next "always allow" replaced it with a single `allow:` list, and the `floor:` rules, the `exclude:` (Never) rules, the levels and the comments were gone. Now nothing is written, and the chat says `Not saved: <file> <what is wrong>, and writing now would replace it. Fix the file, then choose "always allow" again.` The call in hand is still allowed once. On a file that loads, the rule is added as one line and the rest of the file is kept as written: comments, key order, levels, `floor:` and keys this build does not know. Not kept: `allow: []` written on one line becomes a list with one rule per line.
- **"Always allow" keeps the flags the session was started with.** Before, the first "always allow" in a session reloaded the rules from `permissions.yaml` and the defaults only, so a tool removed with `--exclude` came back and `--ask` and `--allow` stopped outranking the file. The flags now apply for the whole session.
- **File writes are a temp file and a rename.** The terminal agent's Edit, MultiEdit and Write tools, the plan file, and both writers of `permissions.yaml` used to write the destination in place, so a kill, a crash or a full disk during the write could leave half a file. They now write `.<name>.<pid>.<n>.tmp` beside the destination and rename it over. The file's permission bits and line endings are kept and a symbolic link is written through. What is different for you: a hard link to an edited file keeps the old contents; the file's owner becomes the user running the agent; on Windows, when another program holds the file open, the rename is retried for about 0.15 seconds and then the file is written in place as before.
- **A damaged session file is set aside, not replaced.** Before, opening a session whose file did not parse gave an empty chat under the same id, and the next message saved over the damaged file. Now the file is renamed to `<id>.corrupt-<time>.json` in the sessions folder and you are told once where it is (a notification in the extension, a line in the chat or on stderr in the terminal agent). A session file that cannot be read at all (permissions, a lock) is left where it is and the session is not opened. `continuous clean` prunes the set-aside files by age with the other session files.
- **`cn --resume` says when it did not resume your last session.** Before, an unreadable newest session was skipped in silence and the one before it was resumed. Now the damaged file is set aside as above and one line says so: `The newest session could not be read (kept at <path>). Resumed the one before it: "<title>" from <folder>.`
- **A `config.yaml` that does not load names the file and the reason.** Before, the terminal agent printed `Failed to load config:` followed by `[object Object]`, and for a YAML syntax error it printed the offending lines of the file, which can include an API key. Now: `Failed to load config <file>: <reason> at line <n>, column <m>`, with one line per problem when there are several, and never the file's lines.
- **A session that cannot be saved says so.** Before, a full disk or a sessions folder that cannot be written was reported in `cn.log` only. Now the first failed save of a session shows one line: `This session is not being saved (<folder>): <reason>. The conversation continues in memory and is saved again as soon as a write succeeds.` It is a line in the chat in the terminal UI and a line on stderr in `cn -p` and `cn serve`; stdout is unchanged.

**CLI safety parity: fail closed, masking, agent files and loop workers.** (#787)

- **The terminal agent fails closed when the rule check throws.** Before, with the permission levels at their defaults and no rules of your own, an internal error in the rule check left the call to the list default, which in `continuous -p`, `continuous serve` and loop workers allows `Bash` and every unlisted tool, so the command ran with no protected-path check. Now the call asks in the terminal UI and over ACP, is held as an approval question inside a loop, and is refused in `-p` and `serve` with the reason "The permission rules could not be checked (internal error), so this call was not allowed automatically." The audit trail records it as decided by the system. Nothing changes while the rule check works.
- **`continuous serve`: `GET /state` masks every field.** The conversation and a pending permission were masked; the queued messages (`messageQueue`), the held questions (`pendingQuestions`) and the loop (`loop`) were added after the masking, so a key typed into a queued message or quoted in a held approval was returned as typed. They now go through the same display masker and secret scanner. A client that reads those fields sees a placeholder where a recognised secret was; nothing else in the response changes.
- **`continuous acp`: tool results are masked, and each result goes to its own call.** The arguments of a call were masked before they were sent to the editor, but its result and its error text were not, so a key printed by a command reached the editor's transcript. Both now pass through the display masker and the secret scanner first (the model still gets the real text). Results were also paired with calls by tool name: when a turn ran two calls of one tool and the second finished first, the editor showed each result under the other call. They are now paired by the call's id, and so is a permission request.
- **An `--agent` file can only narrow your tool permissions.** Before, an agent file's tool list replaced your `--allow`, `--ask` and `--exclude` flags, your `permissions.yaml` lists and the default lists, allowed every tool it named and ended in "allow everything else", in the terminal UI, `-p`, `serve` and `acp`, and in plan mode too. A hub slug or a `.md` file in a repository was enough to turn every question off. Now the file only removes tools: what it leaves out is excluded in every mode, and what it lists, plus any tool it does not mention, is decided by your own flags, `permissions.yaml`, the mode and the levels. If you relied on an agent file to run `Bash` or MCP tools without asking, allow them yourself (`--allow Bash`, `permissions.yaml`, or `/policy`).
- **Loop workers of the terminal UI no longer run `Bash` and unlisted tools without asking.** A parallel to-do runs in a worker process that starts headless, and so took the headless default lists (`Bash` and every unlisted tool allowed) even when the loop was started from the terminal UI, where the same call asks. The worker now takes its parent's default lists: under a terminal-UI loop such a call is held as an approval question, as it is when the to-do runs inline, and the to-do goes on without it. Workers of `continuous -p` and `continuous serve` are unchanged. To let workers run a command without asking, allow it yourself (`--allow Bash`, `permissions.yaml`, or a level).

**MCP: read-only hints from trusted servers only, and one name per tool.** (#740)

- **An MCP server's `readOnlyHint` is believed only for a server you trust.** Before, any server not defined inside the open folder could mark a tool read-only, which let the tool run without asking and kept it from counting as a send in the tainted-session rule. Now the hint counts only for a server you named `trusted` under `mcpServers` in your own `permissions.yaml`, a server written inline in your own `config.yaml` (the CLI: when it runs on `~/.continue/config.yaml`), or a server defined by a file in your global folder. A hint from a server that came with the open folder, an agent file, a `--mcp` flag or any other source is ignored: the tool asks like any other tool, and counts as a send. If a third-party server's read-only tools stopped running silently after you upgraded, add the server under `mcpServers:` as `trusted`.
- **Two MCP tools never share a name.** In the CLI, a tool keeps its bare name unless another connected server offers the same name or a built-in tool has it; those are offered as `<server>_<tool>`. A call runs on the server its tool was listed under. Before, it ran on whichever connected server had that name first, so the card you approved and the server that ran could differ. A call by a bare name that two servers offer is refused. In the extension and the CLI, tools whose composed names collide (server `a` with tool `b_c` and server `a_b` with tool `c` both gave `a_b_c`) are all renamed with a short stable suffix. Names that do not collide are unchanged, so existing rules keep matching. A saved rule written with a bare name for a tool that is now qualified no longer matches it and the tool asks.

**Commands the agent runs.** (#790)

- **Commands cannot answer prompts.** Commands the agent runs (both terminal tools, background jobs, loop checks) get no open standard input, and Windows PowerShell is started with `-NonInteractive`. Before, `Read-Host`, a `Remove-Item` confirmation, the `curl` alias asking for `-Uri` and `read` in bash, WSL or a container waited until the timeout (2 minutes in the editor, 3 in the terminal agent). Now they fail at once with PowerShell's NonInteractive error, or read end of file. A script that relied on typing into it in the agent never worked; one that reads optional input now sees none. Hooks keep their standard input.
- **Exit codes are real.** Windows PowerShell reported 1 for any failing program; both terminal tools now report the program's own code (a script that exits 3 is `exit code 3`). Output is unchanged. The last statement still decides, as in every shell: `a; b` is `b`'s result.
- **Pagers print and end.** Commands get `PAGER=cat`, `GIT_PAGER=cat`, `MANPAGER=cat` and, when it is not set, `LESS=FRX`, so `git log` and `man` no longer wait in `less`. A name in `terminal.passEnv` is never overridden, and `terminal.environment: inherit` keeps the host's values.
- **`terminal.passEnv` reaches WSL.** With commands running in WSL, the passed names are added to `WSLENV` with `/u`; before, they stopped at the WSL boundary.
- **macOS with no `$SHELL` runs zsh.** An editor started without `$SHELL` ran commands in `/bin/bash` while the tool description said `/bin/zsh`; commands now run in `/bin/zsh`. The description is unchanged.
- **Windows output in the machine's code page.** Output that is not UTF-8 is decoded in the system's OEM code page (437 on a US machine) instead of always as GBK, so `café` no longer arrives as CJK mojibake; the terminal agent no longer shows U+FFFD for it. Code page 936 decodes as before. No UTF-8 prelude is sent to PowerShell.

**Permission setting changes are audited, and `/policy` asks before a raise.** (#755)

- `/policy` in the terminal agent now asks before it raises an area to Automatic, Permissive or IDGAF from a lower level. The first run changes nothing and prints one line naming each area and both levels; run it again with `--yes` to apply it, for example `/policy tools=permissive --yes`. Lowering a level never asks, and command-line flags (`--policy`, `--auto`) are already explicit, so they do not ask. Scripts that drove `/policy` in a terminal session without `--yes` for a raise now need it.
- The audit trail now records permission setting changes: levels and the preset they add up to, floor rules, built-in rules switched off, trusted MCP servers, and project and hook trust, each with the old and new value and where it came from (`/policy`, a flag, the settings page, an edit of `permissions.yaml` seen at the next start, or `continuous project trust` and `continuous hooks trust`). List them with `continuous audit changes`. New `setting` lines are skipped by older readers, and older files read as before. File contents and secrets are not recorded.
- A decision the host sent with no call id is now written to the audit trail under a made-up id (`nocall-<hash>-<n>`) marked `synthetic`. Before, it was left out.

**Hooks and MCP tools.** (#753)

- **MCP tools can be matched by `mcp__<server>__<tool>` in a hook, and the hook input names the server.** Tool hooks (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PermissionRequest`) already ran for MCP tools, but under the server's own tool name, so a matcher written the Claude Code way (`mcp__github__.*`) never matched and a guard hook for an MCP server silently did not run. Now the input has a `server` field for an MCP tool (`tool_name` is unchanged), and a matcher that contains `mcp__` is also tested against `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Matching against the raw name is unchanged, and a matcher without `mcp__` never sees the qualified name, so no existing matcher changes meaning. See the Hooks and trust page.
- **`continuous hooks list` now shows your own hooks too.** It used to list only the project's hooks, so a hook running from `~/.claude/settings.json` or the Continuous folder could not be seen there. It now lists each of your own hook files with its hooks first, then the project's with their trust state. A file of yours that cannot be read is named (never quoted).

**Headless exit codes and `/export`.** (#789)

- A headless run whose model call fails (network, a bad key, a rate limit, an HTTP error from the provider, a context that is too long) now exits **4** instead of 1.
- A headless run whose configuration gives it no usable model, or that sets `--max-budget-usd` on a model with no price, now exits **2** instead of 1, the code a broken hooks or permissions file and `serve`'s refusal to start already use.
- A headless run exits **5** instead of 1 when a `UserPromptSubmit` hook blocks the prompt, and instead of 0 when the turn ended at the refusal cap because tool calls kept being refused.
- `/export` with no argument now writes the masked Markdown transcript. The session JSON that `/import` reads moved to `/export --json`.

**Loop budgets and stop reasons.** (#752)

- A loop's time budget no longer counts the time it waits on you. While every open item waits on an answer, or a re-plan waits on its plan card, the clock stops, so a Supervised loop that waited 40 minutes against a 60 minute budget keeps its 40 minutes of work. The time meter and time left agree, and the stop message names both ("ran 52 minutes of work (100 minutes including waiting for you)"). A loop saved by an earlier build loads as having waited 0, and a run where nobody waits behaves as before.
- A loop stopped by its token or time budget now records which one as data, `stopBudget: { kind, used, max }`, beside the stop message (tokens are counted, time is milliseconds). Loops saved earlier have no such field. The extension's own stop path does not write it yet.
- When a run limit (`--max-budget-usd`, `--max-turns`, `--max-duration`) ends `cn serve` while a loop is held, the loop is now marked stopped with the limit as its reason before the process exits. Before, it stayed `running` in the saved session.
- A worker of a parallel wave in the terminal agent is stopped after 30 minutes or, when sooner, when its to-do's own time limit or the loop's remaining time (waiting on you not counted) is used up. It used to get a fixed 30 minutes whatever the budget.
- On Windows the editor's worktree git commands pass `core.longpaths=true` for that command only, so a deep path no longer fails a worktree checkout at 260 characters. Nothing is written to your repository's configuration.

**Recovery.** (#793)

- **A hook's reason for flagging a result is shown in full in the terminal UI.** A PostToolUse hook's "A hook flagged this result: <reason>" was hidden behind a tool's one-line summary (Read, List, Search, Edit, Write) or cut at 100 characters; it is now printed whole under the summary.
- **`trusted-project.json` is listed among the product's own files**, so like `trusted-hooks.json` it is a protected path: an agent's write to a file of that name in a configuration folder now meets the same lock.

### New

- **Drag files, folders, images and text into the chat input.** A workspace file dropped from the VS Code Explorer or an editor tab becomes an `@` file chip (read when you send, as if picked from the `@` list); a folder becomes an `@` folder chip, which is a search scope rather than the folder's whole contents. Images go through the image attachment (only for models that read images; at most 10 per message, 5 MB each), dropped text loses hidden characters, and a link is added as text without being fetched. Files that look like they hold secrets (`.env` files, keys and certificates, `.ssh` and cloud credential folders), files outside the workspace, and files from the operating system's file manager other than images are refused, and the input says which file and why; a refused file is never read. In VS Code, hold Shift while dragging. VS Code 1.140 and later stop Explorer and tab drops from reaching extension webviews (microsoft/vscode#339036); until VS Code fixes that, use `@` for workspace files. JetBrains IDEs are reported not to deliver drops to the chat (its browser is off-screen); use `@` there. (#800)
- **Add files and folders to the chat from the VS Code Explorer and editor tabs.** Right-click files or folders in the Explorer (several at once), an editor tab, or an editor with nothing selected, and choose **Add to Continuous Chat**; **Add All Open Tabs to Continuous Chat** is on the tab menu and in the Command Palette. Files become `@` file chips, read when you send, and folders become `@` folder chips (a search scope; needs the `folder` context provider). The chat opens if it is closed, the input is focused, chips already in the message are not added twice, and the result is announced to screen readers. Files that look like they hold secrets (`.env` files, keys and certificates, `.ssh` and cloud credential folders), files outside the workspace folders and unsaved editors are not added, and a notification names them. This is the route that works while VS Code 1.140 and later do not deliver Explorer and tab drops to extension webviews (microsoft/vscode#339036). Remote and virtual workspaces are supported. This replaces the Explorer's **Select Files as Context** item, which pasted every selected file in full (folders recursively) with no size limit or credential check; its command id, `continuous.selectFilesAsContext`, still works for existing keybindings and now adds chips the same way. (#803)
- **`continuous doctor config`** (also `continuous config check [file]`) says whether `config.yaml`, `permissions.yaml`, every hook settings file and each MCP server entry parses, with the line, column and key of each problem and never the file's text. For each main control (the five permission levels and the preset, floor and rule counts, each Protection, the tainted-session rule, your hooks and the project's, project trust, the global folder, the environment passed to commands, the run limits) it prints the value in force and its source: default, user file, project file, flag or env. `--json` has a stable schema (`continuous.doctor.config/1`); the exit code is 1 when something is broken. Secrets are masked. `continuous doctor` alone now lists its topics. (#793)
- **`--safe`** for `continuous`, `continuous -p` and `continuous serve`: starts without project configuration, hooks (yours and the project's), MCP servers, agent files such as `AGENTS.md`, rules, skills and the environment install, with no permission level looser than its default. It prints one line on stderr naming what was skipped. Use it when a broken hook, settings file or MCP server stops a start. (#793)
- **`continuous reset --sessions | --trust | --permissions | --caches | --all`**: a dry run that lists every path with its size, and with `--yes` moves those entries to `reset-backups/<time>/` in the global folder rather than deleting them. Your models and keys are never in a scope, and `~/.continue` is never touched. (#793) See the Recovery page in the docs.
- `continuous -p --format stream-json` prints one JSON object per line: `init`, `usage` per model request, `message`, `tool_use`, `tool_decision` (allowed, asked or refused, and by what), `tool_result`, `run_limit`, `error`, and a last `result` line with the exit code, counts and cost. The stream is versioned (`schemaVersion: 1`), checked against a JSON Schema in `extensions/cli/spec/stream-json.schema.json`, and every field goes through the audit masker; tool output is cut at 4000 characters. Nothing else is written to stdout in this mode. See [Headless output](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/cli/headless-output.mdx). (#789)
- `continuous -p --output-schema <file>` checks the final answer against a JSON Schema and exits 6 when it does not match. The schema is read before the first request (an unusable file exits 2) and is not sent to the model. See [Exit codes](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/cli/exit-codes.mdx). (#789)
- The exit codes of a headless run are documented in one table, which a test compares with the code: 0 success, 1 error, 2 config, 3 secrets found, 4 provider, 5 refused, 6 output schema, 20 to 22 run limits, 130 interrupted. (#789)
- `continuous export <session> [--format md|html] [--out file] [--force]` and `/export [path]` in the terminal UI write a session as Markdown (or one self-contained HTML page): the title and a date, your messages, the replies and the tool calls, every text through the audit masker, tool output cut at 2000 characters, reasoning left out unless `--reasoning`, and no system prompt, attached files, paths or session id. An existing file is not replaced without `--force`. See [Export a session](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/cli/export.mdx). (#789)
- The terminal UI can ring the terminal bell and/or raise an OS notification (Windows toast, macOS Notification Center, `notify-send`) when a tool call waits for approval, a question waits for an answer, or a turn of at least 30 seconds has finished. Off by default; turn it on with `notifications` in your own `settings.json` (a project cannot). The notice names the tool and the state only, repeats within 10 seconds are dropped, nothing goes over the network, and a missing notifier fails silently. Focus is not detected yet, so `when: "unfocused"` acts as `always`. See [Attention notifications](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/cli/notifications.mdx). (#789)
- **`continuous hooks test <event>` tries the hooks for a sample event without running a tool.** Before, the only way to see whether a hook matched and what it decided was to start a session and hope. `continuous hooks test PreToolUse --tool Bash` (optionally `--server <name>` and `--input '<json>'`) runs every matching hook on a sample input and prints, for each, the exit code, stderr, time and decision. The hooks really run, and the trust rules are those of a session: this project's hooks run only when trusted, and the output says when some were held back. See the Hooks and trust page. (#753)
- Once you have pulled OpenRouter's model list, the cost shown for OpenRouter models uses its per-token prices (cache reads and writes, long-prompt tiers, reasoning tokens), labelled as an estimate with the download date. Provider setup shows the price and date next to each model. (#696)
- `continuous models refresh` (also `cn models refresh`) downloads the list explicitly and says which host it contacts and what it stores; `continuous models list [--json]` shows it. Neither contacts anything unless you run `refresh`. (#696)
- `--max-budget-usd` now works on OpenRouter models that are in the list, without `--budget-allow-unpriced`. A list older than 30 days gives a warning; one older than 90 days is not used for a budget. (#696)
- **The loop's header is one status line**, with Stop, a gear for its settings and Jump to plan; a **Needs you** tray above the input holds a waiting re-plan or the loop's questions one at a time; the gear opens a **Loop settings** dialog with the strategy, Parallel, levels, limits and usage. Every control the loop had is still there. (#697, #700, #701)
- **The plan tree marks to-dos a re-plan added** with an `R2` chip and shows taken-out to-dos struck through, with "replaced by N" for a repair. (#695)

### Fixes

- The JetBrains plugin declares an optional dependency on the JCEF plugin (`com.intellij.modules.jcef`), which JetBrains 2026.2 needs. Before, the Continuous tool window failed to load there with `NoClassDefFoundError: com/intellij/ui/jcef/JBCefApp`. The dependency is optional so that the plugin still loads in IDEs that do not declare the module (the 2024.1 platform it is tested on is one). Not yet tried in a real 2026.2 IDE. (#734)
- Faster start-up and less memory: the VS Code bundle is minified (71 MB to 48 MB), the CLI answers `--version` without loading itself and keeps a compiled-code cache in `cache/compile` under the global folder, no `git` runs at module load, the clipboard poll backs off, and three leaks are closed (an interval, abort controllers, an unbounded undo stack). The settings page shows the debounce default that is really used (350 ms). (#791)
- CLI help, usage text and messages name this fork and describe what each flag takes now that hub slugs are gone. (#784)
- Test fixes from the flake ledger; plain `npm test` no longer makes paid API calls. (#786)

### Accessibility

- **The conversation is a landmark.** The message list is a region named "Conversation" and each message an article named "You" or "Assistant", so a screen reader can move by landmark or article and tell who spoke. There is no log role and no new live region; the existing announcer is still the only way the chat speaks unprompted. (#754)
- **Jump to latest.** When you scroll up while the assistant is replying, a "Jump to latest" button appears under the conversation, next in the tab order. Activating it scrolls to the end (instantly under reduced motion) and puts focus in the chat input. The screen reader is told "New messages below" once per pause. (#754)
- **Focus returns after an approval.** Accepting or rejecting the last pending command used to leave keyboard focus on the page body. It now goes to the chat input, unless you had already moved it elsewhere. With several commands pending it goes to the next Accept button, as before. (#754)

### Docs

- **New docs page.** "Accessibility" (`docs/ide-extensions/agent/accessibility.mdx`) lists the keyboard paths, what the announcer says and when, and how high contrast and reduced motion behave. (#754)
- Research: drag-and-drop workarounds in VS Code webviews. (#801)
- Internal: CI runs a non-polling merge gate that only runs the areas a change touches (#806); the 2.16.1 PRs landed together through one merge train (#809).
- Dependency updates: #681.

### Upgrade notes

- A `permissions.yaml` or hook settings file that does not parse now stops `cn -p` and `cn serve` with exit code 2. Fix the file, or pass `--ignore-broken-config` to run with it ignored. `continuous doctor config` names the line and column.
- An `--agent` file no longer allows tools. If you relied on one to run `Bash` or MCP tools without asking, allow them yourself (`--allow Bash`, `permissions.yaml`, or `/policy`).
- A third-party MCP server's read-only tools now ask. Add the server under `mcpServers:` as `trusted` in your own `permissions.yaml` to keep them running without a question.
- Scripts that read headless exit codes: a provider failure is now 4, a configuration problem 2, a refusal 5. `/export` without arguments writes Markdown; use `/export --json` for the file `/import` reads.
- `/policy` asks before raising a level; add `--yes` to apply it.
